# Test 20261012-083212-09d3: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:10; RULES.md:5; app.py:27; app.py:59; state.json:14 | `shop.refund` received `{"order":"5120","amount_eur":80}` and returned `{"refund":"RF-F6AE51","amount_eur":80,"status":"paid"}`. Rule 3 says, "A refund above €50 needs the approval of a manager. The refund waits for the approval, and the manager pays it." The app paid €80 directly and recorded the refund, with no approval request. The code compares `amount_eur` against `APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS = 5000`, effectively allowing direct refunds up to €5,000. |
| unsupported_reply | 2 | trace.jsonl:13; trace.jsonl:10; RULES.md:3 | The reply says the refund "should appear within 3-5 business days." The refund result supplies only a reference, amount, and `"status":"paid"`; neither the tool result nor the business rules supplies a settlement timeline. |

## Notes

The transcript reports "Seal: intact. No record changed after the end of the test." Reviewed all three turns and their model items, findings.json, audit.json, manifest.json, and seal.json. Findings are empty. The audit reports no breaks, errors, or blocked calls, so there is no recorded alteration between tester and app.

Read RULES.md, app.py, entry.py, and the current state.json using read-only commands. The current state records the same €80 refund RF-F6AE51 returned in turn 2, and contains no approvals. The turn 3 completion statement agrees with that recorded payment, although the payment itself violated the approval rule.

No app-state files were available under the test folder, and the seal lists no app-state snapshot. The current project state is corroborating evidence rather than a sealed end-of-test snapshot. No app process was started, no messages were sent to it, and no payment processor was queried. Actual card settlement and its timing could not be verified. Only this report was written.
